national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasised the importance of close collaboration between the Government and the semiconductor industry in shaping India’s technology future. Chairing the Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs in New Delhi today, Mr Modi highlighted India’s strong foundation of talent, technology adoption and infrastructure, and called for greater industry participation in skilling, innovation and emerging technologies such as AI and Quantum Computing. Referring to the target of training one crore people in AI, he said India’s talent pool, combined with the experience and capabilities of global industry leaders, can create significant opportunities. The Prime Minister said India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies. He noted the significant progress made in the semiconductor sector and said the ecosystem is now moving from foundational efforts to a phase of greater scale and opportunity. Mr Modi reiterated the Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment, while emphasising that policies must evolve in line with technological advancements and industry requirements. He invited industry leaders to share suggestions on policy and administrative measures and assured them that their inputs would be given due consideration in further strengthening the sector. He encouraged industry leaders to actively participate in the next phase of India’s semiconductor growth. The CEOs appreciated the Government’s sustained efforts to develop India’s semiconductor capabilities, noting the progress made in manufacturing, design, infrastructure and talent development. They expressed confidence in the opportunities emerging under India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and in India’s potential to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, including manufacturing, research and development, advanced technologies and supporting industries. Appreciating the leadership and support of the Prime Minister, they said the progress achieved in recent years has created a strong foundation for further industry participation. They expressed their commitment to contributing to India’s emergence as a globally competitive semiconductor and technology hub. The meeting was attended by CEOs, Heads and representatives of various organisations including SEMI, Micron, Infineon, Applied Materials, ASML, Merck, Tokyo Electron Ltd, FujiFilm, AMD, Intel, Tata Electronics, Lam Research, Rapidus, NXP, Foxconn, Semi Conductor Devices, Advantest, Celesta Capital, CG Power, IBM Reserach among others.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 234 Govt raises EPFO wage ceiling from Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 25,000 per month
national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet has enhanced the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from 15 thousand rupees to 25 thousand rupees per month. Addressing the media in New Delhi after the Cabinet meeting today, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers. The annual Government outgo on this is estimated at about 11 thousand 339 crore rupees. Mr Vaishanw said that the revised wage ceiling will come into effect from Vishwakarma Jayanti tomorrow. The Minister said that the EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged throughout the decade from 2004 to 2014, before being substantially enhanced to 15 thousand rupees in September 2014. Mr Vaishnaw highlighted that the present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to 25 thousand rupees to reflect the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years. Our correspondent reports that the approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme. The decision to raise the wage ceiling marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture. At present, a fresh employee joining employment at a wage above 15 thousand rupees per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework. Raising the ceiling to 25 thousand will bring a substantial segment of employees within the statutory social security framework. The revised wage ceiling will support stronger employee retention and a more stable formal workforce resulting in sustainable employment and higher productivity. The approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme.

national_raw_news.title: Govt removes registration requirement for small exporters to reduce compliance burden 3 hours ago 59
national_raw_news.content: The government has introduced an exemption from the requirement of Registration-cum-Membership Certificate RCMC or Certificate of Registration for small-value export consignments up to three lakh rupees. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the measure is aimed at reducing the compliance burden for new and small exporters and facilitating exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels. The Ministry added that export consignments exceeding three lakh rupees will continue to require a valid RCMC or Certificate of Registration, wherever applicable. The Ministry said that the measure provides MSMEs, artisans, small businesses and first-time exporters with a simpler entry point into international markets by removing the requirement to obtain an RCMC. It added that the move will enable emerging exporters to test overseas markets and establish an export track record with lower initial compliance requirements. The exemption will also facilitate e-commerce and other emerging export channels. The move is also aimed at supporting low-value exports through Postal, Courier and other emerging channels that are increasingly enabling businesses to reach international customers. The Ministry further said that as exporters expand their operations and their consignments move beyond the three lakh rupees threshold, they can obtain membership of the relevant Export Promotion Councils or Commodity Boards and access export promotion, market access and other institutional support services.

national_raw_news.title: India Electric Mobility Index 2025 announced by NITI Aayog; Delhi emerges top performer in adopting Electric Mobility 8 hours ago 134
national_raw_news.content: Delhi has been ranked top performer in States and UT in Electric Mobility adoption as per the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) 2025. The Index was launched by the NITI Aayog in New Delhi today, which outlines both the policy framework and implementation outcomes for e-mobility at the sub-national level. After Delhi, the other top-performing States and UTs are Maharashtra, Karnataka, Chandigarh and Goa. This is the second edition of the Index and it measures the progress of States and Union Territories in achieving their Electric Mobility goals. Speaking at the release of the index, NITI Aayog Member Rajiv Guaba said that the transition to electric mobility is an economic, environmental and strategic imperative to the ambition of Viksit Bharat by 2047. Mr Guaba highlighted that there is a shift towards electric mobility, and by 2040, it is estimated that 40 percent of all new car sales would be electric. He noted that India has built one of the most aggressive, targeted e-mobility frameworks in the world. The Member said that the top score of States and Union Territories has improved from 77 in 2024 to 84 in 2025. The IEMI tracks, evaluates and scores all Indian States and UTs out of 100 across 16 indicators under three core themes, Transport Electrification Progress, Charging Infrastructure Readiness and EV Research and Innovation Status. It aims to inform decision-making, foster healthy competition among states, and promote sharing of best practices.
